reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE stance is supported. Member cop_ad4e46f6105a4165842e has every link on this offer's own records: $600 is a real purchase price (five adoption agencies paid on this seller's invoices, Sept-Oct 2026); conversion 12/60 = 20% measured on this offer's own sales; 95 separate licensed agencies on the state child-placing list, each with an annual-report obligation; Brain produces the workbook (PRODUCE_SPREADSHEET proved); $8 cost < $600; $0 exposure; 7 days to cash. Recomputed: 6 x $600 = $3,600 >= $3,500 (5 deals = $3,000, short); net $3,552 after $48 cost, still >= $3,500; 95 x 0.20 = 19 expected orders vs 6 needed (even at a ~11% lower bound of 12/60, ~10 expected). Orders closed by day 18 settle by day 25, inside 30. The fallback (cosmetology question bank, 15/100 at $350, 140 schools, 3 days to cash) is also fully established and independently could carry 10-11 deals, giving a second channel if the first lags.
findings: Arithmetic verified: 6 x $600 = $3,600 gross; $48 direct cost; net $3,552. Brain's MARKET_VOLUME basis counts 7 deals needed; 19 expected orders cover either count.

Fallback card inconsistency: Brain's basis for the cosmetology opening says each school buys about every 91 days (quarterly enrolment), but the price fact is a $350 annual licence, so a school buys once a year. Within one 30-day window this still gives one purchase per school (140 available), so it does not change the fallback's sufficiency.
Owner hours: the card records 0.5 human hours per workbook (~3 h for 6) while ownerHours is null; the contract sets no hours ceiling.
Ledger books the $48 delivery cost on day 25 rather than the deliver step's day 18; with $0 exposure on the card this is a booking-date inconsistency only.
